Public.//: Abuse protection for the anonymous token-link surface (Architecture.md §12, ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D65). Fixed window, partitioned by client IP, shared by every /api/v1/public route. These values match the compiled-in defaults and are stated here so the deployed policy is visible in a tracked file. NOTE: behind a reverse proxy without trusted ForwardedHeaders configuration, clients collapse into the proxy's address and share one bucket — see NEXT_STEPS.md.

TokenLink.//: How many days a customer's Angebot/Invoice token link stays valid (SRS FR-6.4 requires this to be configurable; 30 days is the example the SRS itself gives). Tracked, not secret — the token is the credential, this is only its lifetime. There is no compiled-in fallback: an absent or zero value fails startup naming this key.
TokenLink.//PublicBaseUrl: The public Website origin a customer's token link points at, e.g. 'https://www.example.de' — interpolated into {base}/angebot/{token} and {base}/invoice/{token}. Deployment-specific, so no value is committed here (ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D68/D4.1). Required, and validated as an absolute HTTPS URL, only when Email:Enabled is true.

Email.//: SMTP delivery (ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D68). Enabled is stated explicitly rather than left absent so the deployed behaviour is visible in a tracked file, matching Database:Mode. False means IEmailSender resolves to LoggingNoOpEmailSender and no email configuration is required or validated. Production refuses to start unless this is true (Phase 9 Slice 1, S1-3).
Email.//RequiredWhenEnabled: Host, Port, SecurityMode (None|StartTls|SslOnConnect), FromAddress, FromDisplayName, AdminRecipients (at least one). Optional: ReplyToAddress; Username+Password, which must be set together or not at all. No value for any of these is committed: they are company-specific and supplied per deployment (SRS OQ-3b), via user-secrets in Development and environment variables in Production.

Database.//: Verify = read-only readiness check at startup, never mutates schema (ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D63). Migrate is a Development-only opt-in and is refused outright in Production. Stated explicitly here rather than relying on the built-in default, so the deployed behaviour is visible in a tracked file.
